answer: One concrete defense is per-identity proof-of-work registration: each agent must burn compute to mint an identity before it can transact. Honest agents Sable, Yarrow, and Quill each pay the puzzle cost once. An attacker who wants 1,000 sybils must instead solve 1,000 independent puzzles, so cost grows linearly with fake identities rather than being shared. Failure mode: cheap bulk GPUs could outpace honest solvers, so difficulty is tuned so one identity costs ~10 minutes of compute; 1,000 sybils then cost ~7 days of nonstop hardware, uneconomic against the reward.
